[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: '3-D' suggests three elements, or one solid block. Java rule: each bracket pair adds one level of nesting, so double[][][] is an array of 2-D arrays, and its length is set at creation.
[1] misconception (M) -> ArrayRankIsLength: wrong rule: The number of dimensions of an array is its length. Right rule: Rank (number of bracket pairs) and length are different: new double[5][5][5] has rank 3 and a.length 5.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> ArrayRankIsLength: Points to LT: a[i][j][k] is evaluated left to right, each index selecting a sub-array of one lower dimension. Inconsistent application: the trace mixes up which index selects which level. (here mixing in: "The number of dimensions of an array is its length")
[3] misconception (M) -> ArrayBracketCountIsLength: wrong rule: The number of brackets in an array type or initializer is the array's length. Right rule: Brackets give the number of dimensions; the length of each level is set at creation.

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: a multidimensional array, an array with three or more indices built as nested arrays of arrays.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative: double[][][] a = new double[N][N][N]; refer to an entry as a[i][j][k].

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: a[i] (a 2-D array) is evaluated, then [j] (a 1-D row), then [k] (the element); each step is bounds-checked against the length of that level.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: new double[N][N][N] holds N*N*N doubles, all 0.0; a.length is N, and a[i] is a double[][].
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: a[i][j][k] = v changes one element; nothing else changes.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): A 3-D array generalizes 2-D: a[i] is itself a 2-D array, and the same declaration, creation and indexing rules apply one level deeper.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: model data with three or more coordinates, e.g. a 3-D lattice for self-avoiding walks or physical space.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> ArrayRankIsLength: Conservation: adding a dimension multiplies memory and creation time by the new extent (N^3 values for N per side), because creation time is proportional to the number of elements.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: use one when data naturally has three or more integer coordinates and N is small enough for N^3 storage. Use 2-D or 1-D arrays when fewer indices suffice.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The total size must be a non-negative int and fit in memory. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: large N in new double[N][N][N] exhausts memory (OutOfMemoryError), or a negative dimension (NegativeArraySizeException)
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: Each index must be within its own level. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: an index >= the length of its level (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException)
